catalog.title: An iid FPP law with proved KPZ exponent relation

primary_target.title: 50 years of first passage percolation
primary_target.location: Question 22, Section 4.3 printed pp.88-89; question also reproduced in summary printed p.147; equation (4.19)
primary_target.exact_question: Find a distribution of passage times where (4.19) holds.
primary_target.version_warning: Both revisions directly checked: the 2015 author-hosted PDF uses (4.13), while arXiv v2 uses (4.19). Do not mix numbering.
primary_target.recovered_model: Ordinary undirected nearest-neighbor FPP on Z^d, d>=2, with one fixed iid nonnegative edge-weight law. Passage times are infima of path sums.
primary_target.quantifiers: Existential in a single law; a witness must specify its dimension, admissibility and exact fluctuation/wandering exponent definitions, prove required existence properties, and prove the identity. Planar values 1/3 and 2/3 are not required by the question itself.
primary_target.recovered_catalog_statement: Exhibit a nondegenerate iid undirected FPP law with well-defined fluctuation and wandering exponents satisfying chi=2xi-1.

conditional_primary.title: The universal relation between scaling exponents in first-passage percolation
conditional_primary.author: Sourav Chatterjee
conditional_primary.scope: For d>=2, nearly-gamma iid weights with an MGF near zero, equality of its upper/lower fluctuation exponents and upper/lower wandering exponents implies chi=2xi-1. Upper definitions use uniform exponential moments over all nonzero lattice endpoints; lower definitions use uniform variance and expected-deviation lower bounds beyond a radius.
conditional_primary.does_not_supply: A concrete iid law for which the two exponent equalities have been established.

additional_primary_checks.scope: Auffinger-Damron prove chi<=2xi-1 under existence of Chatterjee's exponents without the nearly-gamma assumption. This is still a conditional exponent result.

additional_primary_checks.title: Rotationally invariant first passage percolation: Breaking the n/log n variance barrier
additional_primary_checks.scope: Basu-Sidoravicius-Sly (2026) give Var T=O(n^(1-epsilon)) for a rotationally invariant Riemannian planar model. The abstract does not exhibit the fixed iid nearest-neighbor lattice law or exact exponent relation sought by P0110.
